minor_characters.name: Miss Betsy Barker
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 003; the spinster whose Alderney cow falls into a lime-pit and is later dressed in grey flannel on Captain Brown’s advice.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She appears only in a single anecdote that duplicates other, stronger scenes establishing Captain Brown’s practical kindness.

minor_characters.name: Lord Mauleverer
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 004; an aristocratic visitor whom Captain Brown once saved at sea and who dines with the Browns at the Angel.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His cameo flatters Captain Brown’s past but does not affect the plot or any character’s later choices.

minor_characters.name: Major Jenkyns (the Indian cousin)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 005; briefly visits Cranford with his invalid wife and Hindoo servant, largely to fluster Miss Matty’s housekeeping.
minor_characters.reason_removable: This episode is a self‑contained comic interlude that neither forwards Miss Matty’s arc nor connects to Peter’s return.

minor_characters.name: Thomas (the postman)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 015; a kindly, talkative village postman described at length for his holiday rounds and late deliveries.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a color figure whose routines do not influence any major event (bank failure, shop, reconciliations, or returns).

minor_characters.name: Mrs Johnson (the butcher’s wife)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 004; briefly cited as reporting a leg of lamb bought for Lord Mauleverer’s visit.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one‑line reference that can be cut without changing any scene’s stakes or outcomes.

minor_characters.name: Peggy (Miss Betty Barker’s maid)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 009; comic asides and door‑answering at Miss Betty Barker’s tea party.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her business is purely logistical and humorous and can be omitted while retaining the scene’s point and Lady Glenmire’s introduction.

minor_characters.name: Mr Hayter (the rector)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 011; glimpsed at the conjuror’s show surrounded by schoolboys.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He has no bearing on the conjuror/Samuel Brown reveal or on later town resolutions.

minor_characters.name: Farmer Benson and Widow Hayward
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 012; minor victims cited during the robbery scare (apple thefts and missing eggs).
minor_characters.reason_removable: They are illustrative names in the panic montage and can be dropped without affecting the robber‑rumor throughline.

subplots.name: The Alderney cow in flannel
subplots.reason_removable: A charming but redundant vignette of Captain Brown’s common sense; other episodes (old woman’s dinner, smoky chimney) already establish the same trait.

subplots.name: Lord Mauleverer’s two‑day visit
subplots.reason_removable: Shows rank consciousness and hints at Brown’s past heroism, but nothing in the main arc depends on it.

subplots.name: Major Jenkyns’s stopover from India
subplots.reason_removable: A freestanding comic flurry about hosting a gentleman that neither seeds nor resolves any core plot line.

subplots.name: The Headless Lady of Darkness Lane
subplots.reason_removable: The ghost scare is an amusing detour within the robbery panic and can be excised without altering the mistaken‑spy thread or the town’s eventual composure.

digressions.topic: Essay on ‘small economies’ (string, envelopes, butter) and Miss Matty’s candle‑saving habits before the family letters
digressions.reason_removable: A genial essayistic preface that delays Peter’s backstory without revealing character interiority not shown elsewhere.

digressions.topic: On‑stage trick‑by‑trick description of Signor Brunoni’s performance and Miss Pole’s Encyclopædia ‘receipts’ for magic
digressions.reason_removable: Lengthy technical play‑by‑play that can be trimmed while preserving the essential conjuror episode and its spy mistake.

digressions.topic: Thomas the postman’s holiday rounds and Miss Jenkyns’s letter‑timing habits
digressions.reason_removable: A nostalgic side essay that neither advances the bank failure scene nor informs the decisions that follow.

digressions.topic: Tea‑shop minutae about ‘make‑weight’ comfits and peppermints for children
digressions.reason_removable: A humorous operating detail that can be condensed without affecting Miss Matty’s shop arc or the town’s support.
